title: Find out whether a click on a clip piece picks it
goal: A walk that clicks the second piece of a cut recording at a point on its bar ends with nothing picked: the panel loses its Properties section and the bar shows no highlight. It is not yet known whether a person's click does the same or only the walk's click does; find out, and if the app is at fault, make a click on a piece pick that piece.
notes: Seen 2026-10-05 while writing Scripts/playtest/half-speed-reads-alike-walk.json. Repro: openSampleRecording, Cmd 2, select tool, videoSeekMiddle, clipSplit (piece 1 in hand), videoSeekThreeQuarters, then { "do": "click", "at": [1300, 894], "space": "window" } (centre of piece 2 on V1 in the 1728x990 probe window; the same y the right-click walks use, e.g. timeline-right-click-walk [349.2, 893]). log.json for the click: 'at (1300, 894) window = view (1300, 862) handler down 0.3ms up 0.2ms; clipBar bodies 2' and state 'selected': 'nil', 'selection': []. The panel then showed Time (Piece 2 of 3/2 of 2), Captions, Transitions only; with the playhead at the 4s cut it showed the Edit point section instead. A second identical click gave the same state. The piece's tap is ClipPiecesBar .onTapGesture -> EditorState.selectClipPiece (Sources/Photonz/ClipPiecesBar.swift ~400), sharing the piece with .gesture(carry(...)); something under it (a lane background tap?) may be clearing the selection. No existing walk left-clicks a clip to pick it (they rightClick or press by name), so there is no evidence either way. A press by name on 'Tutorial Sample piece 2' left piece 1 in hand. Not reproduced by a person: Ghoztty Accessibility was denied, so no real click could be made.
acceptance: Someone clicks the second piece of a cut recording on the timeline in Photonz Dev and records whether the clip is picked with piece 2 in hand
If a person's click fails, it is fixed so a click on any piece picks the clip with that piece in hand, and a walk proves it with a pointer click at a point on the bar
If only the walk's click fails, the walk harness's click reaches a piece's tap the way a person's does, or the limit is written in docs/design/playtest-harness.md

log.note: owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Reproduced on the probe, 2026-10-05: same setup, walk 'click' at (1300,894) window left nothing picked (selected nil); a 'windowClick' (real press+release posted to the window, hit tested by AppKit) at the same point picked the clip with piece 2 in hand (Properties Piece 2 of 2, clip line 4.0s->8.0s, ring round piece 2). So the app is right and only the walk's click was wrong: 'click' hands its press to the canvas view, which runs under the timeline, and the canvas took it as a click on nothing. Photonz Dev was not touched (runner rule); the window-posted click on the probe is the stand-in for a person's click.

The app was never at fault: a real click posted to the window on piece 2 picks the clip with piece 2 in hand. Only the walk's canvas click failed, because it hands the press to the canvas under the timeline. Fixed in the harness: a click step at a window point covered by chrome now fails, naming windowClick, and a covered point in any other space says so in the log; documented under click in docs/design/playtest-harness.md. New walk a-click-on-a-clip-piece-picks-it-walk (no flags) picks piece 2 then piece 1 with real clicks; it, the 5 walks that click at window or view points, and Scripts/test.sh all pass. Commit d0d6de4b.
